summary: Marswalk Planner is an open-source decision-support tool that helps a human explorer plan and survive a walk on Mars. It fuses multi-mission NASA data into a layered, uncertainty-aware site model of Jezero Crater and computes three routes to any destination — shortest, slope-aware, and a full mission-constrained route — so the trade-offs are explicit. Every route is checked against a hard walk-back constraint: at each point, can the explorer still return to safety on remaining life support, even if the rover is lost? The planner produces a survival envelope (where you can go and still get back alive), avoids rock-hazard fields real slope-only routing would accept, and shows a route-stability map of how often the recommendation changes under terrain-data error. It never presents an unvalidated number as a safety guarantee: missing data is treated as unknown, not safe. This directly answers the “Martian Map” challenge — a fused, explainable, uncertainty-honest map for human EVA planning.
details:
What it does. Marswalk Planner plans and pressure-tests human EVA (spacewalk) and rover routes across a Martian site. For any start→destination it computes three routes — shortest 3-D path, slope-aware, and full mission-constrained — and reports length, time, energy, slope, rock exposure, walk-back margin, and science value, plus the explicit reason any route is rejected.

How it works. The terrain becomes a graph; A* search (validated against an independent NetworkX oracle) finds paths under layered rules. Each data layer is declared hard exclusion, objective cost, or informational. A physics engine models locomotion energy, consumables, and a walk-back gate: time-to-nearest-safe-haven ≤ remaining life support − reserve, tested under contingencies including rover loss and suit degradation. On top we add exact multi-objective planning (NAMOA*, Pareto-validated), time-windowed science orienteering, a rock-hazard detector→planner link, and a route-stability analysis over a DEM-error ensemble.

Benefits & impact. It turns scattered orbital datasets into one explainable, uncertainty-aware map for mission planners — surfacing why the safe route differs from the obvious one. On a real HiRISE boulder field (ESP_017355_2260, 461 boulders) the rock-aware route cut hazard exposure ~98% and changed the path; the survival envelope collapses from 80%→47%→7% of the area under worsening contingencies.

Validity / honesty. The full pipeline runs and is covered by an offline test suite (200+ cases) on synthetic terrain, with two real-data demos (real HiRISE boulders; real AI4Mars terrain patches). Physics parameters are clearly marked placeholders; real-DEM and GPU runs are owner-validated. We never present an unvalidated risk score as a failure probability.

Creativity. Most route planners optimize distance. Ours makes survivability and honesty about uncertainty first-class: the hero output isn’t a line on a map, it’s the zone you can enter and still walk home from — and a map of how much to trust it.

Tools. Python 3.11 (NumPy, Pydantic), A*/NAMOA* planner, FastAPI + OpenAPI service, React/MapLibre web map, PyTorch + Detectron2 (rock detector), NetworkX (test oracle), pytest + ruff + CI. Developed across RTX 4050/3050/GTX-1650 laptops and Apple-silicon Macs.
